title: The transport says the arrow keys step a frame, and with a clip picked they move the clip
goal: The Previous Frame and Next Frame buttons under a recording say they can be pressed with the left and right arrow keys. With any layer picked, which is nearly always while you are cutting, those keys move the picked layer a pixel instead and quietly edit the document. Either the keys should step the playhead while the timeline has your attention, or the buttons should stop promising a shortcut that does something else.
notes:
Found while building the timeline zoom, on 2026-09-22. Not introduced by it.

Reproduction. Scripts/playtest/open-out-the-timeline-walk.json (an earlier draft of it) pressed the right arrow five times with the detached sound layer picked, to step the playhead five frames before a split. What the walk log recorded, step by step:

  [36 appKey] right sent through the app ... tree: Tutorial Sample sound [sound] (1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
  [37 appKey] right sent through the app ... (2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
  ... (5.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
  [43 action] FAILED: there is nothing to split at 4000 ms

The layer moved five points along x. The playhead never moved: it was 4000 ms before the presses and 4000 ms after them.

The rule is deliberate and commented, Sources/Photonz/CanvasKeys.swift:69: the arrows step a frame only where selectedLayerID == nil, so the arrows still nudge a layer somebody has taken hold of. The promise that does not hold is Sources/Photonz/MotionStripView.swift:804 and :810, whose help reads "Back one frame (←)" and "On one frame (→)" whatever is picked.

Worth deciding rather than patching: a nudge is how every layer in the app is moved a pixel, and a frame step is what the arrows mean in every video tool there is. One of the two has to give in a document that has time.
acceptance: With a clip picked on the timeline, pressing the right arrow either steps the playhead one frame or does not move the layer, and whichever it does is what the transport button says it does
The keys still nudge a picked layer in a document with no time in it, which is every screenshot
A walk covers it: it presses the arrow with a clip picked and claims what moved

log.note: Related, from the scrub-audio task on 2026-09-22: dragging the playhead now plays the sound under it (ScrubAudition.swift), but stepping a frame with the arrow keys is still silent. If this task is changing what the transport says about the arrow keys, it is worth deciding at the same time whether a key step should make a sound, and if so when it stops: a key press has no end the way a drag does.
folded into premiere-s-keys-work-on-the-timeline, which owns what the arrows do on the timeline; acceptance carried across
